items.title: Solubility trends of Group II hydroxides and sulphates:

source_refs.note: Solubility trends of Group II hydroxides and sulphates:: a main subheading of 6.9.2 Lattice energy, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 132-133.

blocks.text: ΔH°sol depends on both lattice energy and hydration enthalpy.

items: Look at the solubility trends of group II metal hydroxides. Both hydration energy and lattice enthalpy decreases down the group due to decrease in charge density of group 2 cations. But it is observed that the lattice energy decreases more rapidly in the series Mg(OH)₂, Ca(OH)₂, Sr(OH)₂ and Ba(OH)₂ than does the energy of hydration in ions Mg²⁺, Ca²⁺, Sr²⁺ and Ba²⁺. For this reason, the lattice energy factor dominates this solubility trend. ΔH°sol becomes more exothermic so solubility increase.

Now look at the solubility trends of group II metal sulphates. Because the SO₄²⁺ is much larger than the OH⁻, the decrease in lattice energy going through the series of sulphates from MgSO₄ to BaSO₄ is less, but the energy of hydration of the cation decreases by a greater amount. Now the energy of hydration dominates the solubility trend, and the solubility decreases from MgSO₄ to BaSO₄. ΔH°sol becomes more endothermic so solubility increase.
book_errors: becomes more endothermic so solubility increase

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The sulphate ion is SO₄²⁻, not SO₄²⁺. In the last sentence, a ΔH°sol that becomes more endothermic means the solubility decreases (as the same bullet says: “the solubility decreases from MgSO₄ to BaSO₄”), not increases.
